start.setupTitle: What to set up before scanning
start.setupIntro: Vedette only scans inside the scope you confirmed, and only approved devices. Do these two things in order.
start.stepScope: Enter your network ranges and confirm the scan scope (admin only)
start.stepScopeHelp: Enter the company network ranges and tick the commitment that you may scan those addresses.
start.stepDevices: At least one approved device inside the scope
start.stepDevicesNone: There are no devices yet. Vedette will see devices once the sensor runs, or you can add them by hand on the Devices page.
start.stepDevicesNoneOk: There are devices but none can be scanned yet: approve new devices, or check the network ranges and the exclusion list.
start.noInternal: There are no devices in the inventory yet.
start.title: Choose devices to scan
start.description: Confirmation scans run only checks a person has read, almost all of them GET requests. A check may prove a flaw by reading what it should not (a file through a path traversal, the output of a harmless command such as id); none of them was found to create or change anything or to send anything to anyone else.
start.scope: Confirmed scope: {{networks}}. Vedette never scans any address outside it.
start.commitment: Scan scope commitment ticked on {{date}}, confirmed by {{by}}.
start.noCommitment: The scan scope commitment is not ticked yet.
start.manualNote: Scan now runs immediately, without waiting for the time window ({{from}} to {{to}}): it first identifies each device you picked (open ports, operating system and software versions, with nmap), then checks it at {{rate}} requests per second, following the exclusion list.
start.asIs: Vedette is provided as-is. Its author is not responsible for how you use it.
start.safeNote: Fragile devices (printers, cameras, old NAS) and devices of unknown type are scanned only when you pick them, at a quarter of the speed. Scheduled scans and automatic rescans skip them, and also skip devices you added by hand.
start.noExternal: No public domain or IP yet.
start.externalHint: This version does not scan external targets for vulnerabilities yet. They are listed so you can see which ones will be ready: only domains verified with a DNS TXT record, and IPs this box itself goes out to the Internet with and has seen within the last 30 days.
start.fragileHint: Fragile or of unknown type: scanned only when you pick it, at a quarter of the speed
start.pickFragile: Fragile: pick it to scan at a quarter of the speed
start.pickUnknown: Type unknown: pick it to identify its services (no operating system probe) and scan it at a quarter of the speed
start.pickManual: Added by hand: pick it to scan
start.pickBox: The Vedette box itself: pick it to scan it from the network. Sweeps and schedules skip it; its packages are matched every hour.
start.busy: A scan is already running. Wait for it or press Stop now.
start.engineBusy: The scanner is still finishing the scan you stopped. Scan now works again in a moment.
start.tooMany: A scan can include at most {{max}} devices; {{count}} are selected. Narrow the selection, then scan the rest in a second run.
start.reportBlocked_one: {{count}} cannot be scanned ({{why}}); its row says why.
start.reportBlocked_other: {{count}} cannot be scanned ({{why}}); each row says why.

start.noExternalMatch: No external target matches the search and filters.

safety.adminOnly: Only an administrator can change these settings. You can still read them.
safety.windowDescription: Scheduled scans only run inside this window. A window that crosses midnight (for example 22:00 to 05:00) counts by its start day.
safety.rateHint: Lower is safer for old devices.
safety.exclDescription: Devices or networks Vedette never scans.
safety.exclLabel: One IP or network per line
safety.exclHint: For example 192.168.10.5 or 192.168.20.0/24. The Vedette box needs no line here: it is scanned only when you pick it.
safety.stopDescription: Stop scanning when a device stops responding unusually, so it does not hang.
safety.stopSwitch: Stop automatically when a device does not respond
safety.neverDescription: Applies to every scan and cannot be turned off.
safety.neverHeadline: No changes, no denial of service

never.exploit: Never plants a file, an account or a backdoor and never takes over a device. A check may prove a flaw by making the device read a file or run a harmless command such as id, and keeps the answer as evidence.
never.dos: Never floods a service with requests to bring it down.
never.brute: Never guesses passwords and never logs in with default ones.
never.write: Runs only checks a person has read and found to change nothing (all but a few are GET or HEAD requests): no account, password, setting, file, record or mail is created, changed or deleted, and no service is turned on.
never.tags: Only uses nuclei templates of the kev group that pass Vedette's own filter; templates tagged intrusive or denial-of-service are dropped.

safety.neverLocked: Dangerous checks are removed from this Vedette build; there is no switch to turn them on.
safety.schedDescription: Scan periodically inside the time window above.
safety.nextScannerDown: The schedule is on, but nothing runs while the vulnerability scanner is not available. Check the box's services.
safety.nextBlocked: The schedule is on, but nothing runs until the scan scope commitment is ticked under Devices, Scope and sensors.

auto.title: Rescan when a new KEV appears
auto.description: When CISA adds an actively exploited vulnerability that has a safe scan template, Vedette rescans exactly the devices involved within 60 minutes and alerts you if one is affected.
auto.switch: Rescan automatically when a new KEV has a scan template
auto.offNote: Off: new vulnerabilities will not be rescanned automatically. Vedette still alerts you when a new KEV matches a device by product.

cred.noHosts: No server can be added yet: a server must be in the inventory, approved, and inside the scan scope.
cred.title: Credentialed scan
cred.description: Deep-scan important servers with a read-only SSH account, so Vedette sees real installed package versions instead of guessing.
cred.how: OpenVAS runs in its own container, separate from the confirming scan. You create a read-only account on the target and give Vedette the private key.
cred.privacy: The private key is stored encrypted on the box and never shown again. Vedette only displays its last four characters and never exports it.
cred.prepareIntro: Run the commands one at a time. The account has no sudo rights.
cred.step1: Step 1. Create a key pair (on your admin machine)
cred.step2: Step 2. Create the account on the target
cred.step3: Step 3. Copy the public key to the target
cred.step4: Step 4. Install the public key for the account (on the target)
cred.prepareEnd: Then open the vedette_scan_key file (the private key, without .pub) and paste its content in the box below.
cred.caption: Servers scanned with an account
cred.removeBody: Vedette deletes the stored key. To scan with an account again you must add the key again.
cred.empty: No server is scanned with an account yet.
cred.emptyHelp: Prepare the target, then add the server below.
cred.pickHost: Choose the target server from the list.
cred.keyHint: Paste exactly from the BEGIN line to the END line, or choose the file. The content is masked while you type.
cred.keyTooBig: The file is larger than 16 KB, so it is not an SSH key. Choose the private key file.
